text.en: This Order may be cited as the Companies Act (Amendment) Order, 2019.

the Companies Act, in this Order referred to as the Act, is in subsection ( 1) - {a} by inserting the following new definitions in the appropriate order - " "accounting corporation" means a company approved or deemed to be as an accounting corporation under the Accountants Order, 2010 (S 115/2010); entity" means a public accountant, an accounting corporation, an accounting firm or an accounting limited liability partnership; firm" means a firm approved or deemed to be approved as an firm under the Accountants Order, 2010 (S 115/2010); limited liability partnership" means a limited liability approved as an accounting limited liability partnership under the Accountants Order, 2010 (S 115/2010); "accounting records", in relation to a corporation, includes such working and other documents as are necessary to explain the methods and by which accounts of the corporation are made up; means profit and loss accounts, or income and expenditure and balance sheets referred to in section 122 and includes notes than auditors' reports or directors' reports) attached or intended to be read with any of those profit and loss accounts, income and expenditure or balance sheets;"; {b) by deleting the definition of "Clerk of Council"; (c} by deleting the definition of "general rules"; (d} in the definition of "Minister", by inserting "and Economy" after "Finance"; (e} by deleting the definition of "resolution for voluntarily winding up". of section 20

The Act is amended by inserting the following four new sections after section 100 - "Power of Court to rectify register in respect of company IOOA. (1) it appears to the Court, as a result of evidence adduced by an applicant company, that any particular recorded in a register is erroneous or defective, the Court may, by order, direct the Registrar to the register on such terms and conditions as seem to the Court just and expedient, as are specified in the order and the Registrar shall, on receipt of the order, rectify the register accordingly.

(2) An order of the Court made under subsection (1) may require that a fresh document, showing the rectification, shall be filed by the company with the Registrar together with a copy of the Court and a copy of the Court application. Rectification by Registrar on application IOOB. (1) Notwithstanding section lOOA, an officer of a company may the Registrar in the prescribed form of - (a} any error contained in any document relating to the filed or lodged with the Registrar; or

(b) any error in the filing or lodgment of any document the company with the Registrar.

(2) The Registrar may, on receipt of any notification referred to in ( 1) and if satisfied that - (a} the error referred to in subsection (l)(a} is typographical or in nature; or

(b) the error referred to in subsection ( 1 )(b) is, in the Registrar's opinion, unintended and does not prejudice any person, the register accordingly.

(3) In rectifying the register under subsection (2), the Registrar shall not expunge any document from the register.

(4) The decision made by the Registrar on whether to rectify the under subsection (2) is final. Rectification or updating on Registrar's initiative IOOC. ( 1) The Registrar may rectify or update any particulars or document in a register kept by him, if the Registrar is satisfied that - {a} there is a defect or error in the particulars or document any grammatical, typographical or similar mistake; or

(b) there is evidence of a conflict between the particulars of a or person and -

(i) information in the register relating to that or person; or

(ii) information relating to that company or person from such department or Ministry of the or statutory body or other body as may be prescribed.

(2) the Registrar rectifies or updates the register under

(1), the Registrar shall, except under prescribed circumstances, give written notice to the company or person whose documents or are to be rectified or updated of the Registrar's intention to do so, and state in the notice - {a} the reasons for, and details for, the proposed rectification or updating to be made to the register; and

(b) the date by which any written objection to the proposed or updating shall be delivered to the Registrar, being a date at least 30 days after the date of the notice.

(3) The company or person notified under subsection (2) may to the Registrar, not later than the date specified in subsection (2)(b), a written objection to the proposed rectification or updating of the register.

(4) The Registrar shall not rectify or update the register if the Registrar receives a written objection under subsection (3) to the proposed rectification or updating by the date specified under subsection (2)(b), unless the Registrar is satisfied that the objection is frivolous or vexatious or has been withdrawn.

(5) may rectify or update the register if the Registrar does not receive a written objection under subsection (3) by the date under subsection (2){b).

(6) The Registrar may include such notation as the Registrar thinks fit on the register for the purposes of providing information relating to any or defect in any particulars or document in the register, and may such notation if the Registrar is satisfied that it no longer serves any useful purpose.

(7) Notwithstanding anything in this section, the Registrar may, if the Registrar is satisfied that there is an error or a defect in any particulars or in a register, by notice in writing, request that the company to the particulars or document relate, or its officers, take such steps such time as the Registrar may specify to ensure that the error or defect is rectified. of duty to make returns lOOD. (1) If a corporation or person, having made default in complying with{a} any provision of this Act or of any other written law which the filing or lodging in any manner with the Registrar or the Official Receiver of any return, account or other document or the giving of notice to him of any matter; {b) any request of the Registrar or the Official Receiver to or complete and resubmit any document or to submit a fresh or {c) any request of the Registrar under section 100C(7) to rectify any error or defect in any particulars or document in the register, make good the default within 14 days after the service on the or person of a notice requiring it to be done, the Court may, on an application by any member or creditor of the corporation or by the or the Official Receiver, make an order directing the corporation officer thereof or such person to make good the default within such time as is specified in the order.

(2) Any such order may provide that all costs of and incidental to the application shall be borne by the corporation or by any officer of the responsible for the default or by such person.

(3) in this section shall limit the operation of any written law imposing penalties on a corporation or its officers or such person in of any such default.". of section 103

The Act is amended by inserting the following new section immediately after "Disqualification for persistent default in relation to delivery of documents to Registrar

(1) Where(a} a person has been persistently m default in relation to requirements of this Act; and (b} that person, within a period of 5 years after he has last been adjudged guilty of any offence or has had made against him an under section 100D or 311A in relation to any such relevant of this Act, without the leave of the Court, is a or promoter of, or is in any way directly or indirectly or takes part in the management of a company, he is guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or both.

(2) this Act which requires any return, account or document to be filed with, delivered or sent, or notice of any matter to be given, to the Registrar is a relevant requirement of this Act for the of this section.

(3) For the purposes of this section, the fact that a person has been in default in relation to relevant requirements of this Act may, to subsection (8), be conclusively proved by showing that, within a of 5 years, he has been adjudged guilty of three or more offences in any such requirements or has had three or more orders made him under section 100D or 311A in relation to those requirements.

(4) A person shall be treated as being adjudged guilty of three or more offences in relation to any such relevant requirement of this Act for the of subsection (3) if he is convicted of any three or more offences by of any contravention of, or failure to comply with, any such (whether on his own part or on the part of any company).

(5) For the purposes of this section, a conviction for an offence section 141C(2)(a} shall not be treated as an offence in relation to a requirement for this Act.

(6) (a} a person has had a third or subsequent order made against him under section lOOD or 311A; and (b} by virtue of the operation of this section that person is disqualified from being a director or promoter of or from being in any way directly or indirectly concerned or taking part in the of a company, in this section shall be construed as preventing that person from with the order of the Court and for this purpose he is deemed to have the same status, powers and duties as he had at the time the act, matter or thing should have been done.

(7) For the purposes of this section, a certificate of the Registrar that a person has been adjudged guilty of three or more offences or has had made against him three or more orders under section 1000 or 311A in relation to the requirements of this Act shall in all courts be received as prima facie evidence of the facts stated therein.

(8) No account shall be taken for the purposes of this section of any which was committed or, in the case of a continuing offence, began the date of commencement of the Companies Act (Amendment)

(9) A person intending to apply for leave of the Court under this section shall give to the Minister not less than 14 days' notice of his intention so to apply.

(10) On the hearing of any application under this section, the may be represented and may oppose the granting of the application.

(11) In this section, "company" includes an unregistered company the meaning of section 192(1) of the Insolvency Order, 2016 s 1/2016).".

HIS MAJESTY

THE SULTAN AND YANG DI-PERTUAN, DARUSSALAM.

( 1) Every corporation which advertises, circulates or publishes any of the amount of its capital which is misleading, or in which the of capital or subscribed capital is stated but the amount of paid-up the amount of any charge on uncalled capital is not stated as as the amount of subscribed capital is stated, and every officer of the corporation who knowingly authorises, directs or consents to such advertising, circulation or publication is guilty of an offence.

(2) person who in any return, report, certificate, balance sheet, statements or other document required by or for the purposes of this Act wilfully makes or authorises the making of a statement false or any material particular, knowing it to be false or misleading or or authorises the omission of any matter or thing without the document is misleading in a material respect, is guilty of an and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $50,000, for a term not exceeding 2 years or both.

(3) Any person who, for any purpose under this Act{a} lodges or files with, or submits to, the Registrar any or {b) authorises another person to lodge or file with, or submit to, the Registrar any document, that document to be false or misleading in a material respect is an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $50,000, for a term not exceeding 2 years or both.

(4) For the purposes of subsection (2), where a person at a meeting votes in favour of the making of a statement referred to in that subsection, he is deemed to have authorised the making of that statement.". of new section 312A
